summary: US-A3: The wallet - a signed-in customer sees their orders and reaches their tickets
description:
**As** a signed-in buyer, **I want** a page listing everything I have bought,
**so that** I can reach my tickets without hunting for the confirmation email.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-221

**Scope narrowed against the epic, deliberately.** TKT-21's COS says the wallet lists "tickets,
passes, lodging and wristbands". Passes (TKT-12), lodging (TKT-13) and wristbands (TKT-15) are
Backlog epics - none of them exist. This ticket lists **orders and their tickets**, which is
everything that exists to list. Building shelves for three things that have no schema is speculative
by definition.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A contract-declared read returns the **completed orders of the authenticated customer**,
  newest first, with a stable cursor for paging (declared, regen committed).
- [ ] **It never returns another customer's orders**, and the test that proves it asks as customer B
  for customer A's data rather than only asserting A sees A's. State the adversary per ADR-021: this
  is an HTTP-caller property, not a claim about anyone with database access.
- [ ] The scan is scoped, not just the result (ADR-019): the filter is index-backed, proven by a
  test on the plan and not only on the rows returned.
- [ ] The response carries what the page needs to link to the **existing** ticket page
  (`/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef]`) - no second ticket-rendering path is built. Note that the order
  ref is a bearer credential (ADR-012): the response is `no-store` and the ref must not reach a log.
- [ ] A storefront wallet page: signed-in only, listing each order with its date, what it is for and
  its total, linking to the tickets; a real empty state for a customer who has bought nothing;
  `Cache-Control: no-store` and **not** in `page-tier.ts`'s cached set.
- [ ] Signed out, the wallet page does not 500 and does not leak - it invites sign-in.
- [ ] Browser-submit verification (AGENTS.md): `make up`, then **submit** the new form(s) in a real browser — the smoke suite only renders, so the whole SSR-rejects-the-write class (origin check, base path, redirect, CSP) is invisible to it. Evidence in the PR. (sign in, buy, see it in the wallet, follow the link to the tickets.)
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** passes / lodging / wristbands (TKT-12, TKT-13, TKT-15 - none exist) - claiming a past
guest order (TKT-223) - re-delivery (TKT-203) - order detail beyond what the list needs (TKT-201).

objective.note: A signed-in customer sees their purchases and reaches their tickets from one page.

scope.note: One scoped read + one page. Narrowed from the epic COS because passes/lodging/wristbands have no schema anywhere in the repo.

uncertainties.note: What 'what it is for' resolves to - commerce holds reservations (slot_id, ticket_type_id) but the human-readable event name lives in catalog. Whether the wallet joins across services or shows only what commerce holds is a plan decision; ADR-004's one-aggregated-call-per-page rule constrains it.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-221 - there is no attribution to filter on until it lands.

approach.note: A keyset-paged read in commerce scoped by the customer column TKT-221 adds, plus an index for exactly that scan; the page reuses the existing ticket route rather than rendering QRs again.

first_slice.note: This is the COS the epic is judged on - it is the first user-visible payoff of the two slices before it.

success.note: Deterministic: A sees A's orders, B is refused A's, the query plan uses the index, the page renders and links.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages - it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it.

governingAdrs.why: Cuts the system at five services + a stateless gateway. Customer accounts must land inside an existing service or the deviation is recorded as an ADR - ADR-042 rejected a sixth identity service and rejected giving the gateway a database.

The precedent AND its reasoning: staff accounts in catalog because catalog owns organizers; the SSR app owns the session, not the service; sessions in-process and unpersisted; per-principal session cap is what bounds the map; the cookie is path-scoped because storefront/scanner/admin/api share ONE origin. It also records that Astro's `security.checkOrigin` CANNOT be turned on behind the gateway (the Node adapter compares against the container Host) - a proxy-aware origin check replaces it.

The rule for where a guard lives: declared `security:` guards operations in a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline `X-Internal-Token` check guards its INTERNAL surface. Commerce's 404-on-internal is load-bearing (it matches the gateway edge-deny), not cargo. Whichever surface customer register/authenticate lands on, this decides how it is guarded.
Contract-first: any new operation is declared in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code is committed before the gate runs.
A scoped read is only scoped if an INDEX backs the filter; proving it takes two tests - the result is scoped AND the scan is.

`guest_order_ref` is a BEARER credential for the ticket bundle (`/api/access/orders/{ref}/tickets` needs nothing else) and is never logged - TKT-202 is an open bug where the gateway logs it. Anything that surfaces or accepts an order ref inherits both properties.

Name the adversary before claiming a security property. 'A customer cannot see another customer's orders' means an unauthenticated or differently-authenticated HTTP caller - it says nothing about anyone with database access.
Response drift fails closed: a handler whose response does not match the declared schema is refused, so a new operation's schema must actually match what the handler writes.

Catalog public read cache / the minutes tier. Per-customer HTML is never cacheable: signed-in pages must answer `Cache-Control: no-store` and must not enter `web/storefront/src/lib/page-tier.ts`'s CACHED_PAGE set.

reference.summary: BLAST RADIUS - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` (compose.yaml `&go-env` anchor) is ONE shared value across all five Go services: whatever holds it can call commerce's /internal/orders/{id}/refunds, inventory's /internal/operational-holds and /internal/slots/{id}/capacity-adjustments, and access's refund surface. The storefront must NEVER receive it.
BLAST RADIUS - `COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` opens commerce's staff refund (money-moving). Held today only by the back office. The storefront must NEVER receive it.

The storefront container today has exactly ONE env var: `GATEWAY_URL`. It holds no credential of any kind and serves anonymous internet traffic. Any design that hands it a token is a new trust decision that must be argued, not assumed.

Precedent to mirror, not to copy blindly: staff sign-in is catalog `staff_accounts` (migration 0015, bcrypt + tripwire CHECK + non-empty-Down refusal), `services/catalog/internal/store/staff.go`, `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go`; the SESSION lives in the back-office Astro process (`web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`, `gate.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`) - opaque 256-bit token, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, absolute 8h TTL, per-principal cap of 5, cookie scoped to `/admin` NOT `/`.

The ticket page this wallet links to already exists and already handles voided/exchanged tickets: `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro` reads `/api/access/orders/{ref}/tickets`. Do not build a second one.
OPEN BUG, same credential class: TKT-202 - the gateway logs `guest_order_ref`, which ADR-012 says is never logged. Do not add a second logging site for it.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-222

**Branch:** `TKT-222-wallet` off `origin/main` @ `cb019de5` (TKT-221 merged as `5bba9427`).
**Routing:** plan = `gpt-5.6-luna` · planReview = `main-agent` · implement = `main-agent` ·
aiReview = `gpt-5.6-luna`. Cross-model invariant checked both ways. No substitution.

**Blockers:** TKT-221 — **resolved** (merged, Done). Zero open blockers.

**Selection reason:** the only claimable child of TKT-21; TKT-223 is blocked by this one.

**Gate waiver:** the owner waiver recorded in full on TKT-220 applies. The `overrides:` list in this
ticket's closeout is its audit record.

### Risk verdict: **`risk:low` NOT claimed**

The carve-outs it hits:

1. **Auth** — the whole ticket is one authorization claim: *a customer sees their orders and nobody
   else's*. That is the deliverable, not a side effect.
2. Likely **>5 files** (contract, handler, store read, index migration, storefront page, tests).

Not a money path — nothing here writes. Not a data migration in the risky sense, though an **index**
migration is likely (see below). Auth is anticipated by the ticket, so this proceeds under the waiver.

### Context-mémo re-resolved at claim — two ADRs have landed since the bake

Both are TKT-220/221's and both constrain this ticket directly:

- **ADR-049 + its TKT-221 amendment.** Customer accounts live in commerce; the storefront holds the
  session; a commerce-signed **customer assertion** proves who the caller is, presented in
  `X-Customer-Assertion`. **That is the mechanism this read has to use** — there is no other way for
  commerce to know who is asking, and the storefront still holds no service credential.
  The amendment also says plainly: `GET /orders/{id}` reports `customer_id` and is **informational,
  not an ownership check** — TKT-222 "must not treat it as one".
- **`orders.customer_id`** exists, nullable, NULL = guest, and **has no index** — deliberately, with
  ADR-019 cited: an index is justified by the scan it removes, and this is the ticket that issues the
  scan.

Rest of the governing set: **ADR-019** (a scoped read is only scoped if an index backs the filter,
and proving it takes two tests — the result is scoped *and* the scan is), **ADR-021** (name the
adversary), **ADR-012** (`guest_order_ref` is a bearer credential and is never logged — TKT-202 is
the open bug where the gateway logs it via the path), **ADR-004/006/045** (per-customer HTML is never
cacheable), **ADR-009**, **ADR-022**, **ADR-028**, **ADR-002**.

**Scope narrowing carried from decomposition, restated because it is the epic's COS:** TKT-21 says
the wallet lists "tickets, passes, lodging and wristbands". Passes (TKT-12), lodging (TKT-13) and
wristbands (TKT-15) are un-started Backlog epics with no schema anywhere. This lists **orders and
their tickets**, which is everything that exists to list.

## 1 Decision summary

1. **Public commerce read guarded by the customer assertion.** Add a contract-declared `GET /customers/{id}/orders` on the public commerce surface. The storefront cannot reach `/internal/` and must not receive a service credential. Resolve identity with existing `customerFromRequest`; missing or invalid assertions return `401`, never guest data. A valid assertion for B requesting A’s path returns `403`; a holder of A’s valid bearer assertion receives A’s orders. Per ADR-021, this protects against HTTP callers, not database writers.

   Cost if wrong: an internal route is unreachable from the storefront, while a credential in the storefront expands the trust boundary to anonymous internet traffic.

2. **Keep the path customer ID, but treat it only as a selector.** The assertion remains the authority. The handler must compare the path UUID with the resolved assertion UUID before querying the store. This directly supports the required B-as-caller/A-as-target test and makes accidental cross-customer reads fail closed. A `/me/orders` route would remove the mismatch branch, but would weaken the explicit authorization test and make resource selection less inspectable.

   Cost if wrong: trusting only the path recreates the `getOrder` mistake; trusting only the assertion makes a regression in caller/resource selection harder to expose.

3. **Use a partial composite index and prove both result and scan scope.** Add a commerce migration creating a plain index equivalent to:

   `orders(customer_id, updated_at DESC, id DESC) WHERE status = 'completed'`

   The production query must filter by `customer_id` and `status = 'completed'`, join the matching reservation, and keyset-page on `(updated_at, id)`. The result-scope test seeds A, B, and non-completed poison rows. The plan test uses the exact production SQL, a large irrelevant fixture, `force_generic_plan`, and asserts the named index plus `customer_id` in the `Index Cond`, following the existing `explainGenericPlan` / `assertReachesVia` precedent.

   Cost if wrong: a correct result can still scan every order; an output-only test would pass against the defect ADR-019 exists to prevent.

4. **Use an opaque composite keyset cursor.** Sort newest first by the completion-time value already maintained in `orders.updated_at`, then `orders.id DESC` as the tie-breaker. Return `limit + 1` rows, emit only `limit`, and encode `(updated_at, id)` in an opaque `after` cursor. Newer concurrent inserts appear on a fresh first page and do not duplicate or disturb rows after an already-issued cursor.

   Cost if wrong: copying cancellation-refunds’ UUID-only `after_order_id` cannot represent ties in a date sort; offset paging duplicates or skips rows under concurrent completion.

5. **Aggregate catalog display data once per wallet page.** Commerce owns the wallet query and returns reservation identifiers and money snapshots. It then makes one bounded, deduplicated internal catalog call for the page’s `(slot_id, ticket_type_id)` pairs and requested locale. Catalog resolves event and ticket-type display names from its own tables, including archived historical rows, using existing primary/relationship indexes. Do not call the existing per-ID `getPublishedPerformance` / `getTicketType` endpoints in a loop, and do not make storefront fetch the global public event list.

   Cost if wrong: commerce-only output cannot satisfy “what it is for”; per-order catalog calls create a cross-service N+1 and global catalog reads violate ADR-004/ADR-019 intent.

6. **Return the existing bearer reference and link the existing ticket page.** Each wallet row carries `guest_order_ref`, integer `total_amount`, `currency`, completion date, event name, and ticket-type display name. The storefront links to the existing `/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro`; it does not render tickets or QR codes. The API and page are `no-store`, and no raw response/body or bearer reference is logged. The shared request logger must also close the known TKT-202 path disclosure before claiming the end-to-end logging criterion.

   Cost if wrong: a second ticket-rendering path duplicates access security and QR logic; logging the ref turns a no-store bearer credential into a durable credential disclosure.

7. **First failing test per layer.** Contract: the route and response are absent from the declared OpenAPI surface. Commerce API: a valid request without an assertion must first fail as `401`. Store: the customer-scoped query must first fail by returning B’s rows for an A/B fixture or by producing a non-index-scoped plan. Catalog: the bulk resolver must first fail if it makes more than one lookup per page or omits archived/name-localization behavior. Storefront: the account page must first fail if it renders without `no-store`, leaks the assertion, or fails to render the empty state. Smoke/browser: the real signed-in page must first fail if the submitted sign-in does not reach the wallet or the wallet link does not reach the existing ticket page.

   Cost if wrong: tests can prove happy-path rendering while missing the authorization, query-plan, cache, and SSR seams.

## 2 ADR

Amend `docs/adr/ADR-049-customer-identity-and-storefront-sessions.md` with a TKT-222 wallet subsection. Record:

- the assertion as the sole commerce identity source for the read;
- the path UUID as a checked resource selector, never authority;
- `401` for absent/invalid assertions and `403` for assertion/path mismatch;
- the single internal commerce-to-catalog display aggregation;
- `guest_order_ref` as a bearer credential, with `no-store` and logging prohibition.

Do not create a new ADR. ADR-019, ADR-004, ADR-006, ADR-012, ADR-021, ADR-022, ADR-028, ADR-043, and ADR-049 already govern the required decisions.

## 3 Definition of Done

1. The OpenAPI contract declares the authenticated, customer-scoped completed-order read, including bounded `limit`, opaque cursor, locale, response fields, and declared error responses; regenerated code is committed.

2. A request authenticated as B cannot return A’s orders, and the negative test explicitly requests A’s path with B’s valid assertion. The claim is documented as an HTTP-caller property, not database tamper resistance.

3. The commerce query is backed by the named partial composite index, and both result scope and physical scan scope are proven with tests.

4. Pagination is keyset-based, newest first, stable across identical timestamps through the order-ID tie-breaker, and does not use offset paging.

5. The wallet response contains localized event/ticket display data obtained through one aggregated catalog call per page, without cross-service database access or N+1 lookups.

6. Each response row contains the existing `guest_order_ref`, and the storefront links to `/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef]` without creating another ticket-rendering path. The ref is not logged.

7. `/[locale]/account` lists date, purpose, and total for every order; `/en` and `/fr` contain all wallet and empty-state strings.

8. A customer with no completed orders sees a real localized empty state.

9. Account HTML and commerce wallet responses return `Cache-Control: no-store`; the account route remains outside `page-tier.ts`’s cached set.

10. Signed-out access redirects/invites sign-in without a 500 or order data leak.

11. The real stack is started with `make up`; a real browser submits sign-in and reaches the wallet, follows a wallet ticket link, and verifies the signed-out path.

12. Regeneration is committed before `make check`, and `make check` passes.

## 4 Files

### Contract and generated code

- `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` — declare the customer order collection, cursor, locale, response, and error shapes.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerate from the commerce contract.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/commerce-api-types.gen.ts` — regenerate storefront commerce types.

### Commerce

- `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` — register and handle the assertion-guarded read; reuse `Router`, `registerRoutes`, `write`, and `customerFromRequest`.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/server_test.go` — route, assertion, mismatch, status, response, and catalog-call-count tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/customer.go` — add the customer-scoped completed-order read beside the existing customer store operations.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/customer_test.go` — store-level query/cursor behavior where suitable.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/attribution_smoke_test.go` — real-Postgres ownership, completed-status, tie, cursor, and scan-scope tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/attribution_invariant_test.go` — retain the source invariant proving no order write updates `customer_id`.
- The next numbered file under `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/` — add the out-of-band partial composite index; do not edit migration `0016_order_customer_attribution.sql`.

### Catalog aggregation

- `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` — add the credential-guarded hand-mounted bulk display read alongside the existing internal routes and `guardInternalSurface`.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` — assert one bounded bulk lookup, locale fallback, archived-row resolution, and internal-token refusal.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/store.go` — extend the catalog persistence port with the bulk display lookup.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go` — implement one SQL lookup over requested slot/ticket-type pairs.

### Storefront

- `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/account/index.astro` — fetch the wallet with `Astro.locals.customer.assertion`, render rows, links, and empty state, and set `no-store`.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/customer-api.ts` — add the server-side authenticated wallet read; never expose the assertion to browser props.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/locales.ts` — add wallet, order, total, date, ticket-type, and empty-state strings in English and French.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/format.ts` — add localized order-date formatting while keeping money in integer minor units.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/page-tier.ts` — verify the account path remains outside `CACHED_PAGE`.
- `web/storefront/test/format.test.ts` — date and integer-money formatting assertions.
- `web/storefront/test/middleware-page-tier.test.ts` — account HTML remains `no-store`.
- `web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts` — one commerce read and one catalog aggregation per page.
- `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro` — retain as the sole ticket-rendering destination; no QR logic change.

### Bearer-reference logging

- `shared/go/obs/requestlog.go` — redact known ticket/order-reference path shapes.
- `shared/go/obs/requestlog_test.go` — assert the bearer reference is absent while ordinary request paths remain logged.

### Live verification

- `smoke/customer_accounts_test.go` — gateway reachability, authenticated wallet response, B-for-A denial, empty wallet, and no-store assertions.
- `smoke/smoke_test.go` — reuse existing gateway/response helpers; no new service credential.
- `compose.yaml` — verify unchanged: storefront keeps only `GATEWAY_URL`, commerce already has `CATALOG_URL` and the shared internal token.

## 5 Test plan

### Contract seam

- The first assertion that fails: the contract validator rejects or 404s `GET /customers/{id}/orders` because the operation is not declared.
- Assert the declared response accepts the complete wallet shape and rejects undeclared fields/statuses.
- Assert missing assertion is handled by the commerce handler as `401`, so the header remains operationally required without making OpenAPI validation turn absence into an unrelated `400`.

### Commerce API seam

- First failure: a request with no assertion returns anything other than `401` with no order body.
- Assert a valid A assertion can read A’s completed orders.
- Assert B’s valid assertion requesting A’s path returns `403` and does not call the store.
- Assert the existing public `getOrder` path remains informational and is never used as the authorization check.
- Assert catalog failure does not return a partial wallet row with a misleading purpose.

### Commerce store seam

- First failure: the result includes B’s order, a guest order, or a non-completed order when listing A.
- Seed completed A, completed B, A guest, and A non-completed orders.
- Assert newest-first ordering and integer amount/currency preservation.
- Seed identical completion timestamps and assert the UUID tie-breaker yields every row once.
- Insert a newer completed order between page requests and assert the existing cursor page neither duplicates nor loses rows after the cursor.
- Assert the cursor is opaque to the response consumer; only commerce decodes it.

### ADR-019 scan proof

- First failure: the plan contains a sequential scan or lacks `customer_id` in the index access condition.
- Use the exact production query, not a copied reduced query.
- Seed enough same-customer and foreign-customer rows that a sequential scan is the wrong planner choice.
- Use the repository’s generic-plan preparation pattern and assert the named partial index reaches `orders`.
- Separately assert the poison customer’s rows are absent from the returned page.

### Catalog aggregation seam

- First failure: one wallet page triggers one catalog request per order.
- Assert the request contains deduplicated bounded slot/ticket-type pairs and locale.
- Assert event and ticket-type names resolve for both `en` and `fr`, with the repository’s locale fallback behavior.
- Assert archived catalog rows remain resolvable for historical orders.
- Assert invalid or missing internal credentials are refused before request binding/lookup.

### Storefront unit seam

- First failure: the page accesses the wallet without using the server-side session assertion or serializes the assertion into rendered HTML.
- Assert `page-tier.ts` returns `no-store` for `/en/account` and `/fr/account`.
- Assert `formatMoney` receives integer minor units and the new date formatter renders both locales.
- Assert the page renders an empty state for `orders: []`.
- Assert each row links to the existing ticket path with the encoded `guest_order_ref`.
- Assert no wallet page code logs upstream response bodies or refs.

### Smoke and browser seam

- First failure: the wallet route is edge-denied, returns a cacheable response, or renders without the signed-in order.
- Through the gateway, create/sign in a customer, exercise an attributed completed order, and assert the wallet response contains only that customer’s completed order.
- As B, request A’s wallet path with B’s assertion and assert `403`/no A data.
- Assert a newly registered customer sees the empty state.
- Assert signed-out `/en/account` and `/fr/account` redirect to the localized sign-in page.
- Run `make up`; in a real browser, submit the existing sign-in form, load the wallet, click a wallet ticket link, and verify the existing ticket page.
- Inspect gateway/service logs after the flow and assert the known `guest_order_ref` is absent.

## 6 Risks and traps

- Do not add a service credential to the storefront. Its `environment:` contract is intentionally only `GATEWAY_URL`.
- Do not use `getOrder`’s `customer_id`; its own code documents that field as informational.
- Do not change checkout attribution or completion writes. `attribution_invariant_test.go` scans `orders` writes, and `customer_id` is written once at order claim.
- Do not backfill pre-0016 orders into accounts; `0016` explicitly treats them as guests.
- Do not use `guest_order_ref` as an ownership key. It is a bearer ticket-retrieval credential.
- Do not use offset paging or copy `after_order_id` from cancellation-refunds; the wallet sort has a timestamp and tie-breaker.
- Do not make the plan assertion against a hand-copied query or a tiny fixture; both produce green but meaningless evidence.
- Do not call catalog once per order or use the global public event list as a hidden join.
- Do not filter catalog display data to published rows; historical wallet entries must still have a purpose.
- Do not introduce floating-point money values. Keep amount/currency as integer minor units plus ISO currency.
- Do not put the account route into `CACHED_PAGE`; per-customer HTML stays outside the cache tier.
- Do not run the new index through server startup; ADR-022 requires the commerce migrate job to apply it out of band.
- `TKT-202` is a real blocker to the literal no-log claim: the shared request logger currently records paths, and the existing ticket URL contains the bearer ref. Either include the narrow redaction in this implementation or do not claim the logging acceptance criterion is complete.
- A storefront restart clears the in-memory session Map; browser verification must account for that and sign in after the stack is stable.

## 7 What this constrains downstream

TKT-223 must claim only an unattributed order whose `customer_id` is still `NULL`, under a transaction that prevents two claims from winning; it must not repoint an attributed order, use `getOrder` as authorization, or key the wallet on `guest_order_ref`. The wallet’s customer index, cursor, response field, and existing ticket link become the read contract that claiming must populate without changing. Changing the route shape, removing the bearer reference, or replacing live catalog resolution with commerce snapshots later would require coordinated contract, generated-code, storefront, and migration changes.

## 8 Follow-up tickets to file

- Historical wallet display snapshots if product requirements later demand the event name as purchased rather than the current catalog name.
- Shared/revocable customer sessions if the storefront grows beyond one in-memory replica.
- Assertion renewal or password-recovery flow; the current assertion/session lifetime is fixed at eight hours and the existing ADR records no recovery path.
- Explicitly track TKT-202 as a prerequisite or include its path-redaction fix in TKT-222; do not leave the bearer-reference logging gap implicit.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial plan critique — by `main-agent` (config.models.planReview)

Cross-model invariant held. Every file, symbol and seam checked against **HEAD**.

**Existence check — all verified.** `customerFromRequest` (`assertion.go`) · `guardInternalSurface`
(`catalog/internal/api/server.go:211`) · `explainGenericPlan` / the generic-plan discipline
(`catalog/internal/store/season_smoke_test.go:204`) · `page-call-budget.test.ts` ·
`attribution_invariant_test.go` · commerce migrations stop at `0016`. No hallucinated seams.

Two things it got right that a plausible plan would have got wrong, accepted explicitly: it found
that the assertion is the **only** identity commerce has and did not invent a second mechanism; and
it refused to call catalog per order, naming the N+1 before anyone could ship it.

---

### F1 — [blocking] `updated_at` is a mutable column and cannot be a keyset cursor

The plan sorts and pages on `(orders.updated_at, orders.id)`, describing it as "the completion-time
value already maintained in `orders.updated_at`". It is not a completion time and it does not stay
put. Counted from the tree, production code writes `updated_at=now()` on at least six paths:

- `server.go:920` — every checkout **retry** on an existing order ("reopening an existing order is
  fresh activity on it");
- `server.go:966`, `:1067`, `:1277` — the `payment_unknown` and `confirmation_pending` transitions;
- `store/recovery.go:148` and the cancellation-refund runner.

A keyset cursor on a mutable key is broken by construction: a row whose key moves **jumps pages** —
it can be returned twice or skipped entirely, and a refund six months later reorders the wallet.

**Amendment:** page on **`orders.created_at DESC, orders.id DESC`**. `created_at` is set by the
INSERT default and no production statement updates it (checked: the only `created_at=` write in
commerce is `cursor_created_at` on an unrelated table). It also means the right thing — when the
buyer bought — where `updated_at` means "when anything last happened to this row". The index must
match.

### F2 — [blocking] The plan absorbs TKT-202, which belongs to TKT-202

`shared/go/obs/requestlog.go` — redacting bearer-reference path shapes — is an open, unclaimed,
unshaped ticket (**TKT-202**: *"the gateway logs guest_order_ref, which ADR-012 says is never
logged"*). Doing it here means changing a logging component **every service in the repo** uses, from
a wallet ticket, in a diff that would then span three modules — and silently closing a ticket nobody
prioritised.

The AC asks that **this response's** ref not reach a log. It does not: the wallet API path carries no
ref, and the response is `no-store`. Following a wallet link to `/[locale]/tickets/{ref}` logs the
ref via the URL path — which is **exactly TKT-202, already true today** from the guest flow, and not
made worse by this ticket.

**Amendment:** out of scope. Say so in the DoD, cite TKT-202, and state the residual rather than
quietly fixing it.

### F3 — [blocking] Cut the catalog endpoint in half

Accepting the shape — one internal bulk read, guarded by `guardInternalSurface`, called once per
wallet page — is right. But the plan specifies resolving **`(slot_id, ticket_type_id)` pairs** with
localized ticket-type display names *and* archived-row handling *and* locale fallback. That is a
second service's contract, handler, store port and Postgres query, all inside a wallet ticket that
also ships a scoped read, an index with a plan proof, and a page.

The AC says the row shows **"what it is for"**. The event answers that. A buyer looking for their
tickets needs to know *which show*, not which fare class.

**Amendment:** the resolver takes **slot ids only** and returns the event's localized name and the
performance start. Ticket-type display names are dropped from this ticket. Keep the one detail that
is not optional and that the draft was right to flag: the resolver must **not** filter on published
state — a wallet is mostly *past* purchases, and a resolver that only sees on-sale performances is
one that goes blank exactly where it matters.

### F4 — [blocking] A mismatch must answer 404, not 403

`GET /customers/{A}/orders` presented with B's valid assertion returning **403** confirms that
customer A exists. That is an account-existence oracle reachable by anyone who can register once —
smaller than ADR-049 §2's registration oracle, and free to avoid.

**Amendment:** answer **404**, identically to an id that does not exist. The handler still compares
the path id against the assertion — that check is three lines and it is what the AC's required
"B asks for A's data" test exercises — but the *answer* discloses nothing. Note the precedent:
commerce already answers 404 rather than 401 on its internal surface, and ADR-043 records that
choice as load-bearing for the same reason.

(I considered `/customers/me/orders`, which makes the whole class impossible rather than tested. It
is the better design in isolation and it is rejected here for one reason: the AC explicitly requires
a test that *asks as B for A's data*, and under `/me` that test cannot exist. Defence in depth plus
the required test beats impossibility plus a weaker test — but if a later ticket revisits the route
shape, this is the trade to reopen.)

### F5 — [non-blocking] Name ADR-020 before someone adds CONCURRENTLY

The plan adds an index migration and never mentions **ADR-020**, whose entire subject is that
`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` is **still not adopted** in this repo — its preconditions are
conjunctive and two remain false even after ADR-022 satisfied the first. An index migration written
without that citation is one somebody "improves" with `CONCURRENTLY` at review time.

**Amendment:** plain `CREATE INDEX`, with ADR-020 cited in the migration comment.

### F6 — [non-blocking] The plan proof cannot be shared, and that has to be said

`explainGenericPlan` lives in `catalog/internal/store`'s **test** package. Commerce is a different
module and cannot import it. ADR-019 is explicit that forking the helper "is how one copy quietly
stops asserting anything" — so a commerce copy needs a comment saying the duplication is **forced by
the module boundary, not chosen**, and pointing at the original.

The parts that must survive the copy, because they are the whole value: `PREPARE` + `SET LOCAL
plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan` + `EXECUTE` **in one transaction** (a `SET` on `*sql.DB` can
land on a different pooled connection), and the check that the parameter survives as `$1` rather
than a literal — without which the plan is a *custom* plan and the assertion proves nothing.

### F7 — [non-blocking, accepted] Sizing

Two services, a migration, a plan proof, a page, and copy in two locales. F2 and F3 remove roughly a
third of it. What remains is at the top of one reviewable PR and is not splittable without leaving a
half — a read nothing renders, or a page with no names.

---

### Pre-mortem

1. **The plan test passes and proves nothing** — a custom plan with the literal substituted, or an
   EXPLAIN through the driver rather than PREPARE/EXECUTE. The precedent's own comments say this
   happened before; copying the helper without its reasoning is how it happens again.
2. **The wallet is empty for every old order**, because the catalog resolver filters on published
   state. F3.
3. **Rows duplicate across pages** after a refund or a retry touches `updated_at`. F1.
4. **The account page renders the assertion into the HTML** — it is on `Astro.locals.customer` now,
   and a debug-shaped `{JSON.stringify(customer)}` in a template ships a bearer credential to the
   browser.
5. **The empty state is never seen**, because every fixture buys something first. It is an AC and it
   needs its own test.

### Verdict

**Accept with amendments.** Four blocking (F1–F4), all fixable inside the plan; F1 is a real defect
in the design rather than an omission. No re-draft needed.

### Decisions made by the agent in place of Gate 2

**D1 — `created_at` as the sort key (A1).** The critique recommends it. There is no `completed_at`
on `orders`, and adding one would be a migration plus a backfill decision this ticket does not need:
`created_at` is set by the INSERT default, no production statement updates it, and it means *when the
buyer bought*. *Cost if wrong:* an order created and completed far apart sorts by creation. For a
checkout that completes in seconds, that is the same thing.

**D2 — Keep the path id, answer 404 on mismatch (A4).** Both halves recommended. The AC requires a
test that asks *as B for A's data*, which needs an addressable A. 404 keeps that test while
disclosing nothing.

**D3 — Ticket-type names dropped (A3).** The critique recommends it. "What it is for" is answered by
the event. *Reversibility:* adding a field to a response is additive; removing one is not — so
shipping fewer fields is the reversible direction.

**D4 — The catalog resolver is `/internal/`-guarded, not public.** Neither document said which
explicitly. Chosen because it is the only option consistent with ADR-043 (an inter-service read is
not part of catalog's public contract) and because catalog's `guardInternalSurface` already
authenticates that whole surface — so it inherits the guard rather than adding one. Commerce already
holds `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CATALOG_URL`; the storefront gains nothing and still holds no
credential.

**D5 — Locale reaches catalog as a request parameter, not a commerce concern.** Commerce forwards
the wallet request's locale and stores none. Most reversible: no locale ever persists in commerce, so
nothing has to be migrated when the supported set changes (it is data, not schema — TKT-36).

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

1. **The `created_at` sort key (A1/D1)** — the largest, and it is a correctness fix to the draft's
   design rather than a refinement.
2. **404-instead-of-403 (A4/D2)** — changes an observable API answer.
3. **Two scope *removals* (A2, A3)** — which no code review will see, because a removal leaves no
   diff. Recorded here because this is the only place they exist.

All except (3) land in the diff and get a genuine second read at `ai-review`.
